thread:
samir: quick heads up — our us-west4 GPU pressure spiked this morning. A bunch of incoming jobs are waiting ~10m because scheduler is trying to pack onto H100 nodes that are currently full while A10G nodes sit at 60%.
priya: ugh, that sounds like mixed-sku scheduling mismatch. which pools are we running? any taints/labels to separate infer vs embed? :thinking_face:
samir: current pool 'gpu-general-usw4' is mixed A10G + H100 (no taints), we used it to save quota. pods request `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` only, no preferred nodeAffinity. autoscaler is set to `balance-similar-node-groups: false`.
ben: that explains it — CA will scale the group but if pods need H100-specific runtime (we saw some pods with model pinned to h100-optimized image) they won't land on A10G. two options: split into sku-specific pools or add `nodeSelector`/affinity to pods.
lina: quota side — subnet in us-west4 is short on IPs. if we create a new sku-specific pool we'll need more secondary IP capacity or a different subnet. current NAT gateway SNAT port exhaustion risk too if we add many nodes. checked `gcloud compute addresses` today.
samir: my preference is to create a small dedicated H100 pool (min 2, max 8) and a compact A10G pool for the rest. keep autoscaler profile tighter on H100 (lower min) and more aggressive on A10G. that avoids scheduler fights and reduces cost.
priya: agree. also suggest updating autoscaler flags on the A10G pool: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m` and `--scale-up-delay=0s` for faster reclaiming. for H100 keep `--max-node-provision-time` relaxed.
ben: on networking: we can request +64 IPs in the subnet but that may hit quota. quick workaround is to enable `ip-per-pod: false` for the new pool (use hostNetwork for small infra?) — but that's risky. better plan: provision new /24 in VPC and attach to cluster (secondary range) — I'll open the quota ticket.
jasper: small gotcha — the GPU driver daemonset failed on two nodes last week due to kernel version drift, so when you provision new instance type make sure the node image matches our driver build or add `node-feature-discovery` to label kernel. otherwise GPU pods stay Pending with `FailedAttach`.
samir: thanks. action items: (1) ben to open subnet/secondary-range quota request and NAT port check — target PR by EOD. (2) lina to draft pool sizing: H100 min2/max8, A10G min4/max30 and taints `gpu.k8s.redwood/type=h100:NoSchedule` on H100 pool. (3) jasper to validate driver image compatibility and add node-feature-discovery check to provisioning job. (4) priya to update autoscaler flags for both groups and include `balance-similar-node-groups` for A10G.
ben: opened ticket CLOUD-3187 for subnet/egress quota, added current counts. link: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/CLOUD-3187 :white_check_mark:
lina: drafting infra PR now, will include terraform snippet:
```
resource "google_container_node_pool" "h100_pool" {
  name       = "gpu-h100-usw4"
  node_count = 2
  management { auto_repair = true }
  node_config {
    machine_type = "n2-standard-32"
    accelerators { type = "nvidia-h100" count = 1 }
    labels = { "gpu.type" = "h100" }
    taints = [{ key = "gpu.k8s.redwood/type", value = "h100", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]
  }
}
```
samir: perfect. one more ask — add a small `eviction-buffer` in console routing so latency-critical traffic can fallback to A10G if H100 is saturated (policy: prefer H100, fallback to A10G with quantized model). can we add that to rollout plan?
priya: yes, we'll add a routing policy + metric to Redwood Console. define SLO and fallback thresholds, then canary it.
samir: ty everyone. ping me on the PRs and i'll help with scheduling tests. :rocket:
